item.title: AI Is Starting to Create Jobs in the UK
item.description: Most British businesses say artificial intelligence has created new roles, a Lloyds survey found.

item.title: Bond Yields Are Hitting Multidecade Highs Around the World
item.description: Everything from inflation to the AI boom is pushing borrowing costs higher.

item.title: RBI’s Forex Deposit U-Turn Exposes Wider Communication Gap
item.description: A sudden decision by India’s central bank to end a special incentive for attracting foreign-currency deposits a month ahead of schedule has caught bankers, economists and traders off guard and raised questions about how effectively it was communicating with market participants.

item.title: Alibaba-Backed Robot Maker LimX Said to Plan Up to $300 Million Hong Kong IPO
item.description: LimX Dynamics has confidentially filed for a Hong Kong initial public offering to raise as much as $300 million, people familiar with the matter said, adding to a wave of Chinese robotics companies lining up to go public.

item.title: Rare $1 Billion IPO Rush Seen in Zambia After Election
item.description: Zambia’s stock exchange expects to bring a record $1 billion of initial public offerings to market after this month’s presidential election, as Africa’s second-biggest copper producer benefits from soaring prices for the metal.

item.title: Robot Dogs Make Chinese Billionaire Even Richer Despite US Curbs
item.description: Wang Xingxing, a millennial billionaire at the center of China’s AI push, is set to see his fortune soar even as Washington blocks his company from launching new robot models in the US.

item.title: Ardian Taps UBS to Explore Sale of Swissbit
item.description: Ardian is weighing a potential sale of Swissbit, a provider of industrial data storage and security products, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: Pony AI’s Robotaxi Revenue Reaches Record as Sales Jump 69%
item.description: Pony AI Inc.’s robotaxi sales reached a quarterly high, now accounting for a third of total revenue, with overseas momentum continuing to accelerate.

item.title: Xiaomi Profit Falls After Memory Crunch Hits Smartphone Demand
item.description: Xiaomi Corp. posted profit that fell less than expected, raising hopes it can weather a persistent memory shortage that’s weakened demand for smartphones.

item.title: South African Business Confidence Edges Higher Amid War Headwind
item.description: South African business confidence improved sightly in July, though the economy continues to be affected by inflationary pressures stemming from the Iran war, the country’s main commerce chamber cautioned.

item.title: JPMorgan’s Faller Turns Selective as European Stocks Get Pricier
item.description: Investors should be more selective about European stocks as improving earnings are increasingly reflected in valuations, according to JPMorgan Private Bank’s Madison Faller.

item.title: Dangote’s Nigeria Refinery Secures $400 Million Ahead of $2 Billion IPO
item.description: Investors have committed $400 million to a planned initial public offering by Dangote Petroleum Refinery & Petrochemicals FZE, the continent’s largest crude oil processing plant, which is raising money to expand the facility.

item.title: BofA Poll Sees Few Bears Left as Investors Pile Into Stocks
item.description: Bullish global investors have ramped up their stock holdings to the highest in almost five years, leaving no room for pessimists, according to Bank of America Corp.’s Michael Hartnett.

item.title: Baidu Posts Fifth Straight Sales Drop After AI Lags Rivals
item.description: Baidu Inc.’s revenue fell for a fifth consecutive quarter, reflecting the search leader’s persistent lag in AI development and a struggling advertising business.

item.title: Apple’s Anti-AI Position Suddenly Becomes Stock Market Baggage
item.description: Apple Inc.’s status as an anti-artificial intelligence play helped the stock tear through the first half of the year as investors grew skeptical of the AI trade. But that sentiment has flipped, and the shares are struggling.

item.title: Germany’s Investor Outlook Improves as Economy Gains Traction
item.description: German investor optimism rose more than anticipated, supporting hopes that the long-awaited recovery of Europe’s largest economy may be gaining traction.

item.title: Canadian Home Prices Edged Up in July as New Listings Slowed
item.description: Canada’s benchmark home price rose for the first time in 20 months in July as markets across the country were buoyed by a stronger outlook for the economy.

item.title: Alibaba Shares Jump 5% as Alipay Launches New Merchant Platform
item.description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. shares rose the most in two weeks as the launch of a new ecommerce platform boosted optimism toward the company before its June quarter earnings this week.

item.title: ECB’s Lane Says Inflation to Hover Near 3% for Rest of Year
item.description: European Central Bank Chief Economist Philip Lane said the pace of consumer-price increases is likely to hold “well above” the 2% target in 2026 due to the Iran war.

item.title: India Weighs Sugar Import Duty Cut to Curb Record Local Prices
item.description: India, the world’s second-largest sugar producer, is considering cutting its import duty on the commodity to help curb domestic prices that recently climbed to a record.

item.title: Germany Is Set to Sell 30-Year Bonds at Highest Yield Since 2011
item.description: Germany’s borrowing costs are poised to hit a 15-year high in a major sale of long-dated bonds as investors demand greater compensation for lending to increasingly indebted governments still grappling with inflation.

item.title: Tanker Stops in Hormuz as Iran Raises Efforts to Control Strait
item.description: A fuel tanker trying to enter the Persian Gulf has made an erratic series of turns and come to a halt near Iran’s Qeshm Island, as the country steps up efforts to control the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: More German Companies Are Closing Down Due to Economic Headwinds
item.description: A greater number of German companies closed shop last year in another sign of how challenging conditions and an aging society are taking a toll on Europe’s biggest economy.

item.title: UK Food Inflation at Lowest Since October 2024 as Britons Hunt for Deals
item.description: Food price inflation in the UK slowed to the lowest level in nearly two years, as British shoppers searched for bargains to keep costs down.

item.title: Rising Yields Threaten to Puncture Asia’s AI-Driven Stock Rally
item.description: A rapid climb in Treasury yields is emerging as one of the biggest risks to Asia’s AI-driven stock rally, an uneasy link that highlights technology firms’ vulnerability to elevated borrowing costs.

item.title: US Stock-Index Futures Drop as Bond Yields and Oil Prices Rise
item.description: US stock-index futures fell as rising bond yields and a spike in oil prices unnerved investors.

item.title: Braskem’s Mexico Unit Files for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy in US
item.description: Mexico’s Braskem Idesa SAPI, a joint venture between Brazil’s Braskem SA and the conglomerate of Mexican tycoon Carlos Slim, has filed for bankruptcy protection as mounting financial strain and a worsening liquidity crunch weigh on the company.

item.title: Bridgewater China Withstands July Rout That Left Quants Reeling
item.description: Macro hedge funds in China including Bridgewater Associates LP’s local unit emerged from the July selloff bruised but not defeated, holding on to their annual gains after a wild stock market selloff that pushed other funds into the red.

item.title: UK Payrolls Fall, Vacancies Hit 5-Year Low in Weak Jobs Market
item.description: UK employers shed more workers in July and job vacancies hit a fresh five-year low as demand for staff remained tepid in the face of heightened uncertainty from events at home and abroad.
